title: Quentin and the Thorn
premise: Edmund Halloran, a woman disguised as a male scribe to escape her family's debts to the Thornfell temple, has memorized every smuggler's path through the mountains. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish on the same night, she rescues a wounded stranger named Quentin who turns out to be the exiled true heir of Thornfell — his crown fused to his skull by the usurper's sorcery, which feeds on him nightly. As Edmund guides Quentin through a starless, ward-haunted wilderness toward the old king's hidden vault, they fall in love even as her debt-contract makes her legally the temple's property and his claim makes her a traitor's accomplice. In the vault, Edmund learns the 'thing wearing the crown' is the first king of Thornfell, sustained for centuries by stolen starlight; she must choose between paying off her family's freedom with the vault's treasure or spending it to unbind Quentin and reignite the stars. She chooses Quentin, burns the contract with the last starlight, and together they shatter the ancient crown — leaving Thornfell heirless but free, and the two of them belonging finally to each other rather than to any throne.
about_author: Sebastian Yarrow is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent six years mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about people trapped by obligations they never chose.

chapters.title: The Ledger and the Lantern
chapters.summary: Edmund Halloran, disguised as a male scribe, copies debt contracts in the Thornfell temple by candlelight, secretly sketching smuggler routes in the margins. When the head priest threatens to sell her contract north, she resolves to flee within the month. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: restless dread beneath careful routine.

chapters.title: Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: On the eve of Edmund's planned escape, every star above the Thornfells goes dark at once, and the border wards shriek and fail. The temple erupts into panic; guards seal the gates. Edmund slips out through the crypt passage only she knows. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: A Body on the Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: In the black pass, Edmund finds a man bleeding out beside a shattered wardstone — crowned, though he claims no crown exists. He remembers only his name, Quentin, and a burning weight on his brow. She binds his wounds because leaving him feels like murder. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: reluctant compassion.

chapters.title: What the Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV reveals fragmented memories: a coronation interrupted, a brother's smiling face, molten gold fusing to his skull. Each night the crown drinks something vital from him. He conceals his identity from Edmund, ashamed and afraid she'll abandon him. Emotional beat: isolation and self-loathing.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse at Greywater
chapters.summary: Edmund barges them past a tollhouse using forged temple seals, but the toll-keeper recognizes her handwriting from old ledgers. They flee into the high fells as hunters are summoned — not for Quentin, Edmund realizes, but for her. POV alternates. Emotional beat: the noose tightening around her specifically.

chapters.title: Debt-Bound
chapters.summary: Edmund confesses everything: her name, her disguise, the contract that makes her the temple's property until her family's debt is paid. Quentin, guilt-ridden, offers nothing but honesty about being hunted too. Two liars strip themselves bare. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: shame transformed into fragile trust.

chapters.title: The Shepherd of Hollowmere
chapters.summary: An old shepherd shelters them and recognizes Quentin's face from coins minted twenty years ago — the lost prince. He tells of the Usurper King whose shadow moves independently and whose court never sleeps. Quentin admits the truth; Edmund does not run. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: the terror of being seen.

chapters.title: Riders in the Dark
chapters.summary: Temple hunters catch up. In a starless skirmish among the scree, Edmund kills a man for the first time and freezes; Quentin fights like someone protecting something precious rather than himself. They escape, but the shepherd is taken. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: guilt and the cost of survival.

chapters.title: The Map Only She Knows
chapters.summary: Edmund leads them onto an unmapped goat-track through the Widow's Teeth, her childhood knowledge becoming their lifeline. For one day, above the cloud line, they laugh, and something unspoken settles between them. Then Quentin collapses — the crown feeding harder as they near the old capital. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: borrowed joy before the fall.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing His Crown
chapters.summary: Quentin dreams fully for the first time: the first king of Thornfell, centuries old, sustained by devoured starlight, wearing each heir's body until it fails. The stars didn't go out — they were eaten. He wakes screaming Edmund's name instead of his own. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: horror of being a vessel.

chapters.title: Sanctuary Refused
chapters.summary: They reach a rebel holdfast hoping for aid, but the rebels want to display the 'dead prince' as a banner. Quentin refuses to be a symbol; Edmund backs him, burning her last bridge with the resistance. They leave as fugitives from every side. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: loyalty chosen over safety.

chapters.title: The Priest's Bargain
chapters.summary: Captured briefly by temple forces, Edmund is offered her family's freedom if she delivers Quentin to the Usurper — the temple has served the crown-thing for generations. She signs nothing, escapes through a latrine chute, and steals back her own contract in the process. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: temptation faced and refused.

chapters.title: Ashfall Vale
chapters.summary: Wounded and starving, they shelter in a valley where the crown's hunger has already killed everything green. Quentin begs Edmund to leave him and save herself; she answers by teaching him her smuggler's maps, making him co-author of their route. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: love declared without saying it.

chapters.title: The First King's Vault
chapters.summary: Following a riddle in Quentin's fused memories, they find the hidden vault beneath the ruined summer palace: treasure beyond reckoning, and shelves of starlight sealed in glass — enough to buy a hundred families' freedom, or to fuel one great working. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: awe curdling into an impossible choice.

chapters.title: Two Debts
chapters.summary: Edmund calculates: the starlight could pay her debt and free her family forever — or unmake the crown and restore the stars, but then the temple will own her until she dies. Quentin, feverish, tells her to take the gold. She almost does. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh — duty against love.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Court
chapters.summary: The Usurper King arrives at the ruins with his shadow moving wrong behind him, offering Quentin his body back in exchange for surrender — the crown-thing merely wants a healthier vessel. Quentin sees his brother's face in the offer and nearly kneels. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: the seduction of easy restoration.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Quentine refuses — not for the kingdom, but because Edmund taught him he belongs to himself first. The Usurper's shadow attacks; the vault begins collapsing. Edmund seizes the case of starlight as they flee deeper into the mountain. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: defiance kindled by love.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: In the vault's deepest chamber, Edmund performs the unbinding using her scribe's knowledge of the old contracts — she rewrites the crown's binding as a debt, then declares it paid, shattering the glass starlight into Quentin's brow. The crown cracks. The first king screams across centuries. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: climax — her inheritance of words becomes liberation.

chapters.title: Stars Returning
chapters.summary: Above the shattered peak, the stars come back one by one. Quentin, crownless and scarred, is only a man — no longer heir to anything. The Usurper, cut off from the crown-thing's power, crumbles to dust mid-decree. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: grief and light arriving together.

chapters.title: The Empty Throne
chapters.summary: Thornfell's lords quarrel over a vacant throne and come seeking Quentin. He publicly renounces the crown, declaring the debt of kingship unpaid and unpayable. Some call it madness; Edmund calls it the sanest act she's witnessed. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: freedom chosen over destiny.

chapters.title: Paid in Full
chapters.summary: Edmund returns to the temple with a handful of remaining starlight — just enough to burn her contract before the high priest's eyes. Her family is freed; she owes nothing to anyone. The temple, its patron gone, begins dismantling itself. POV: Edmund. Emotional beat: vindication and release.

chapters.title: The Road They Make Together
chapters.summary: Spring comes to the Thornfells. Edmund and Quentin walk the smuggler's roads openly, mapping new passes for refugees and travelers, belonging to no crown, no ledger, no one but each other. On the highest ridge, under a full sky of returned stars, they stop running. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: home found in a person, not a place.
